# Command-Line Help for `rtf`

This document contains the help content for the `rtf` command-line program.

**Command Overview:**

* [`rtf`↴](#rtf)
* [`rtf fetch-supergraph`↴](#rtf-fetch-supergraph)
* [`rtf top-operations`↴](#rtf-top-operations)

## `rtf`

A swiss army knife for testing the Apollo Runtime

**Usage:** `rtf <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `fetch-supergraph` — Download and resolve the config required to run a single supergraph under router-scale. The config file generated by this command is mostly a stub containing default values, to generate the full config for a router-scale test please run the 'prepare' subcommand
* `top-operations` — Pull details of the most common operations for a given supergraph from studio and generate mock request data for each one



## `rtf fetch-supergraph`

Download and resolve the config required to run a single supergraph under router-scale. The config file generated by this command is mostly a stub containing default values, to generate the full config for a router-scale test please run the 'prepare' subcommand

**Usage:** `rtf fetch-supergraph [OPTIONS] --graph-id <GRAPH_ID> --variant <VARIANT>`

###### **Options:**

* `--graph-id <GRAPH_ID>` — The graph-id to download
* `--variant <VARIANT>` — The variant of `graph-id` to download
* `--out-dir <OUT_DIR>` — The directory to write output to

  Default value: `output`
* `--staging` — Attempt to pull supergraph details from the staging instance of studio rather than prod



## `rtf top-operations`

Pull details of the most common operations for a given supergraph from studio and generate mock request data for each one

**Usage:** `rtf top-operations [OPTIONS] --graph-id <GRAPH_ID> --variant <VARIANT>`

###### **Options:**

* `--graph-id <GRAPH_ID>` — The graph-id to find operations for
* `--variant <VARIANT>` — The variant of `graph-id` to pull operations for
* `-n`, `--n-operations <N_OPERATIONS>` — The number of operations to pull

  Default value: `20`
* `--skip-mutations` — Whether or not to include mutations as part of the generated request data (The rehydrate tool used by router-scale defaults to skipping)
* `--out-dir <OUT_DIR>` — The directory to write the generated request data to

  Default value: `output`
* `--staging` — Attempt to pull supergraph details from the staging instance of studio rather than prod
